title: Language tasks beyond chat
hook: Labeling, extracting, summarizing, translating and finding similar text. The cheapest good tool for each.
inPlainWords: Chat is one use of language models. Many jobs are narrower: label a text, pull out names and numbers, shorten it, translate it, or find similar texts. Naming the task tells you the cheapest good tool.

useCase.title: Process 30,000 ShopEase tickets a week
useCase.story: Each week the tickets must be labeled by topic, stripped of order numbers and names, summarized for a manager, and replies translated into five languages. Volume is high and the budget is watched.

approaches.name: Rules and patterns
approaches.what: Match exact patterns like formats and word lists.
approaches.greatWhen: Order numbers, emails and fixed phrases.

approaches.name: Classic text ML
approaches.what: Count words and train a simple model.
approaches.greatWhen: Topic labels with plenty of tagged examples, at low cost.
approaches.example: A topic classifier trained on 10,000 tagged tickets.

approaches.name: Fine-tuned small language model
approaches.what: Adapt a compact pretrained text model to one task.
approaches.greatWhen: High volume, one narrow task, and you need speed and low cost.
approaches.example: A small model that tags topics in milliseconds.

approaches.name: Prompted large language model
approaches.what: Describe the task and let a large model do it.
approaches.greatWhen: Low volume, changing tasks, or several tasks with one model.
approaches.avoidWhen: Huge volume, where cost and delay add up.
approaches.example: Summarize a long ticket thread for a manager.

approaches.name: Specialized services
approaches.what: Ready-made services for translation, speech or entity extraction.
approaches.avoidWhen: Domain jargon they do not know, or strict data rules.
approaches.example: A translation service for five languages.

approaches.name: Embeddings and similarity search
approaches.what: Find texts that are similar in meaning.
approaches.avoidWhen: You need a label or a decision.
approaches.example: Find tickets similar to this one.

challenge.question: Which mix is best for the weekly job?

options.text: Rules for order numbers, a small tuned model for topics, a prompted large model for summaries, and a translation service for languages
options.why: Each task gets the cheapest tool that does it well.

options.text: A large prompted model for everything
options.why: Simple to build, but costly and slow at 30,000 tickets.

options.text: Train a giant model from scratch

bestCase.title: Right-size the tool for each language task
bestCase.example: Rules mask order numbers and names. A small model tags topics in milliseconds. A large model summarizes only long, escalated tickets. A translation service handles five languages. The weekly bill is a fraction of the all-large-model option.

worstCase.title: One big model for every job
worstCase.example: A large model is prompted for every label on all 30,000 tickets. It works, but the bill is huge, responses are slow, and label wording drifts from week to week.

route.travelling: Ticket: "Order #48213 lost, third time I'm asking!!"

steps.label: Strip personal details
steps.goes: Rules mask the order number and name.

steps.label: Label the topic
steps.goes: A small model says Delivery, fast and cheap.
steps.goesWrong: A large model is prompted for every label on all 30,000 tickets, and the bill is huge.

steps.label: Summarize for the manager
steps.goes: Only long, escalated tickets get a summary.

steps.label: Translate the reply
steps.goes: A translation service handles five languages.

takeaway: Name the language task first. Use rules for exact patterns, small models for volume, and large models for flexibility.
